脈.meaning: Standing on the <part>moon</part>, an astronaut looks back at Earth through her telescope and spots a <part>river delta</part> splitting into a hundred blue threads, swelling and shrinking as the tide rolls in. 'It's alive,' she whispers. The planet has a <kanji>vein</kanji>, and it's pumping.
脈.on: Back at base, the only plant on the station is a sli<sound>my</sound> <sound>yuc</sound>ca, and even its leaves have little throbbing veins.
脈.kun: She traces the branching rivers in soy sauce across a plate of <sound>su</sound>shi, then in mud on the door of a <sound>jee</sound>p: a line.

債.meaning: At a fancy party, a guest borrows a fur coat and pins an IOU to the empty <part>coat hook</part>, promising to pay double next year. Next year he doesn't, so the host pins the <part>blame</part> on him in big red letters. That IOU is now a <kanji>bond</kanji>, and it grows every winter.
債.on: He pays it off at last in jugs of <sound>ci</sound>der, one for every year he was late.

各.meaning: At the family picnic, every cousin brings a <part>folding chair</part> and a <part>mouth</part> full of opinions, and nobody can hear a thing. Grandma bangs a spoon and sorts it out: one chair, one sandwich and one turn to talk for <kanji>each</kanji>.
各.on: The dog under the table gets a picked-clean chicken <sound>carc</sound>ass all to himself.
各.kun: Then it rains on every one of them. '<sound>Oh</sound> <sound>no</sound>, <sound>oh</sound> <sound>no</sound>!' cries each cousin in turn.

築.meaning: An old granny turns up her nose at <part>commonplace</part> bricks. She saws <part>bamboo</part> on her <part>workbench</part> and lashes it, pole by pole, round the <part>tree</part> in her garden, until her tree house pokes through the clouds. At ninety, she still loves to <kanji>build</kanji>.
築.on: Her cement is <sound>chick</sound>pea mash, and somehow it holds.
築.kun: A <sound>ki</sound>wi bird helps her weigh down the top floor with <sound>zu</sound>cchinis.

没.meaning: A paper <part>maiden</part> cut from a birthday card is set afloat on a puddle as a boat. The first <part>water drops</part> of rain soak her skirt, she curtseys lower and lower, and glug, under she goes. Paper dolls, it turns out, can <kanji>drown</kanji>.
没.on: A <sound>bo</sound>nsai on the windowsill watches, then sneezes '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' in the damp air.
没.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' gasps the girl, and fishes the soggy doll out with a twig from the <sound>bo</sound>nsai.

鳴.meaning: A shy <part>bird</part> can't make a sound, so a lipstick poster lends it a huge red <part>mouth</part> on a stick. It holds the mouth up to its beak, and out comes the loudest, sweetest little <kanji>chirp</kanji> in the park.
鳴.on: Everyone follows the sound through the hedge <sound>ma</sound>ze to find the singer.
鳴.kun: Its reward is a crumb of warm <sound>na</sound>an, which makes it sing all over again.

従.meaning: A little goat with tiny <part>horns</part> rides the <part>chairlift</part> up the mountain, and a <part>giant boot</part> stomps up the slope right below it. When the goat rides down, the boot stomps down. Wherever it goes, the boot will <kanji>accompany</kanji> it.
従.on: At the top they share a picnic, and the boot shakes a shiny <sound>jew</sound>el out of its laces for the goat.
従.kun: A <sound>shee</sound>p, a <sound>ta</sound>co seller and a walking bulb of <sound>ga</sound>rlic fall in behind them, obeying every step.

拠.meaning: Halfway up an ice wall, a climber jams an <part>anchor</part> into a crack, then has to <part>dispose</part> of everything heavy: her snacks, her flask, a spare boot. Lighter now, she wedges her toe on the anchor and breathes. She's found a <kanji>foothold</kanji>.
拠.on: At the top, a tiny <sound>kio</sound>sk is selling hot chocolate, as if it had been waiting for her.
拠.kun: She leans her whole weight on the anchor and eats a pot of <sound>yo</sound>gurt: she relies on it.

模.meaning: A lazy painter can't be bothered to wait for a real <part>sunset</part>, so he paints one on a board and props it behind a <part>tree</part>. Birds fly home early, and the owls get up confused. Not bad for a cheap <kanji>imitation</kanji>.
模.on: A <sound>mo</sound>le pops up beside the tree and paints a copy of the copy on its molehill.

承.meaning: A tiny king says his bath is <part>complete</part> only with <part>three</part> rubber ducks. The butler hates ducks and longs to argue, but he sighs, runs the <part>water</part> and drops in one, two, three. In the end he bows and goes along with it: he'll <kanji>acquiesce</kanji>.
承.on: The ducks bob and spin like a little water <sound>show</sound> for the king.
承.kun: Then the king wants <sound>u</sound>don, a <sound>ke</sound>ttle and a <sound>ta</sound>co, and his baby sister wails '<sound>Ma</sound>! <sound>Wah</sound>!' The butler bows to every wish: humbly received.

聖.meaning: A <part>king</part> gives up his crown, climbs a hill and sits there for forty years with one <part>ear</part> turned up to the clouds and his <part>mouth</part> shut tight, so as not to miss a word from the sky. Pilgrims tiptoe up to look. He's become truly <kanji>holy</kanji>.
聖.on: The pilgrims leave their gifts in a little steel <sound>sa</sound>fe beside him.
聖.kun: One pilgrim limps up in a high <sound>hee</sound>l, one drives up in a <sound>jee</sound>p, and one swims all the way from a coral <sound>ree</sound>f, just to see the saint.

勇.meaning: A skinny <part>male</part> mouse spots the last <part>pizza wedge</part> on the kitchen floor, right under the cat's nose. He takes a deep breath, tiptoes in, grabs the slice and sprints off while the cat snores on. The whole nest cheers his <kanji>courage</kanji>.
勇.on: That night he's crowned a hero and rides round the nest on a toy <sound>u</sound>nicorn.
勇.kun: Fired up, he plans his next raid: an <sound>ee</sound>l in the fridge and a tin of <sound>sa</sound>rdines.

輸.meaning: A farmer needs to get her apples to a market on the moon, so she drives her <part>car</part> straight into the hold of a <part>spaceship</part>. It blasts off with the car, the apples and the farmer still at the wheel. She calls it express <kanji>transport</kanji>.
輸.on: Tucked among the apples is one <sound>yu</sound>zu fruit, a gift for the moon's grocer.

練.meaning: Every morning a puppet master faces <part>east</part>, ties a <part>thread</part> to each finger and makes his puppet dance as the sun comes up. Ten thousand sunrises later, the puppet still trips on step three. It needs more <kanji>practice</kanji>.
練.on: A little <sound>wren</sound> sits on the puppet's hat, practising its own song each morning too.
練.kun: Afterwards he knots a fresh <sound>ne</sound>t of strings for tomorrow, and they train again.

盤.meaning: The town's best <part>carrier</part> is a waiter who balances one <part>dish</part> on his head, one on each hand and one on each knee. At last his boss hands him something wide and flat to hold them all. It's his first <kanji>tray</kanji>, and he weeps with joy.
盤.on: The first thing he carries on it is a single sticky <sound>bun</sound>, like a crown jewel.

怒.meaning: A <part>guy</part> at the fair wins a squeaky toy <part>heart</part> and squeezes it all the way home on the bus: squeak, squeak, squeak. On the fortieth squeak, the lady beside him turns red, steam shoots from her ears and she bites the heart in half. She's very <kanji>angry</kanji>.
怒.on: A <sound>do</sound>lphin on the poster above them seems to grin.
怒.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' says the guy, and hides behind a stuffed <sound>ko</sound>ala until she calms down.

詞.meaning: A film <part>director</part> hates every <part>speech</part> his actors give, so he snips the script into single slips, throws them in the air and makes the stars read whatever lands on their nose. The film makes no sense, but it wins a prize for its <kanji>words</kanji>.
詞.on: The lead actor catches all her lines on a knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld.
詞.kun: In the next scene, a <sound>ko</sound>ala reads them off a <sound>to</sound>tem pole at a <sound>ba</sound>rbecue.

沈.meaning: A <part>sleeper</part> dozes off on an air mattress in the pool. One by one, <part>water drops</part> creep in through a tiny leak, and the mattress sags lower and lower while he snores on, until only his nose pokes out and he wakes with a splutter. The ducks watched him slowly <kanji>sink</kanji>.
沈.on: He bobs up with pool water dripping off his <sound>chin</sound>.
沈.kun: His bed<sound>shee</sound>t and a <sound>zu</sound>cchini-shaped pool toy go down right after him.

陽.meaning: A grey, rainy town hires a weather wizard. He climbs the tallest roof and waves a yellow <part>pennant</part> at the clouds, and they part like curtains. <part>sunbeams</part> pour down on every wet cat and sad umbrella. The town basks in <kanji>sunshine</kanji> at last.
陽.on: Kids rush outside to spin their <sound>yo</sound>-yos in the light.
陽.kun: The sun tickles a sleeping cat's belly until it squeaks '<sound>Hee</sound>!'

層.meaning: Diggers start below an old <part>flag</part> on a hill. Each spade goes further back: last year's snack wrappers, the town as it was <part>formerly</part>, ancient coins, then dinosaur toes, all stacked like a cake. Every slice is a new <kanji>stratum</kanji>.
層.on: At the very bottom they find a fossil bar of <sound>soa</sound>p, still a bit slippery.

陰.meaning: The summer fair is too hot to stand in, so someone ties a big <part>pennant</part> and a <part>kite</part> to a pole to make a patch of cool. 'Right <part>now</part>!' everyone shouts, and they all squeeze under it. Forty people, one thin strip of <kanji>shade</kanji>.
陰.on: A boy knocks over a pot of <sound>in</sound>k, and the dark strip looks darker still.
陰.kun: In the strip, a <sound>ka</sound>rate teacher naps, and a <sound>ge</sound>cko naps on his black belt.

河.meaning: A tiny stream begs the mountain for permission to grow. The mountain nods its <part>approval</part>, and <part>water drops</part> pour in from every hill and cloud until the stream is a mile wide, with ferries and islands. Now it's a <kanji>large river</kanji>.
河.on: The first fish to move in is a golden <sound>ca</sound>rp the size of a ferry.
河.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>lm old ferryman rows across, until the carp splashes him: '<sound>Wah</sound>!'

妙.meaning: A <part>woman</part> paints pictures on grains of rice, using only a <part>few</part> hairs from a mouse's whisker as her brush. One grain shows a whole city at dusk, with tiny lit windows. You need a magnifying glass to see it. Every grain is <kanji>exquisite</kanji>.
妙.on: She keeps her smallest brush tied to a sli<sound>my</sound> <sound>yo</sound>-yo, so she never loses it.
妙.kun: Her finest grain shows a <sound>ta</sound>co beside a tiny <sound>e</sound>gg, painted in gold.

微.meaning: Halfway up a <part>mountain</part>, a <part>chairlift</part> carries a single glass snowflake to an art show. It sits on a velvet <part>stool</part>, and an attendant waves a paper <part>fan</part> to keep it cool, not too hard, not too soft. One breath could crack it: it's that <kanji>delicate</kanji>.
微.on: A <sound>bee</sound>tle rides on the next chair, holding its breath the whole way up.
微.kun: At the top, an ice <sound>ca</sound>rp and a plate of <sound>su</sound>shi wait, giving off a smell you can barely notice: faint.

腕.meaning: A postman is handed a letter whose <part>address</part> just says 'The Man in the <part>Moon</part>'. No rocket, no ladder, so he rolls up his sleeve and reaches up, past the clouds and the satellites, and pops it through the moon's letterbox. That's one long <kanji>arm</kanji>.
腕.on: Back at the sorting office he arm-wrestles everyone, and he has <sound>won</sound> every match since.
腕.kun: He slurps a bowl of <sound>u</sound>don, then reaches across town to pass it to his <sound>de</sound>ntist.

握.meaning: A storm hits the harbour, and the little corner <part>shop</part> starts sliding toward the sea. The shopkeeper hurls a ship's <part>anchor</part> out the door, it hooks a bollard, and he hangs on with both hands as the till rolls past his feet. He never loosens his <kanji>grip</kanji>.
握.on: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' cries the <sound>coo</sound>k from the café next door, clinging to his frying pan.
握.kun: His fist is so tight that the sewing <sound>nee</sound>dle and the bike <sound>gea</sound>r he was holding get squashed flat.

致.meaning: An old-fashioned actor climbs onto a podium, flicks open a lace fan and declares, 'Thou art late, and the king doth frown!' He talks like this at the shops, at the dentist, at bedtime. Whatever he does, he doth.
致.on: Only a <sound>chee</sound>tah in the front row claps, very fast.
致.kun: 'I shall humbly do the washing up,' he bows, then squeals '<sound>Ee</sound>!' at a <sound>ta</sound>co stuck to the pan.

封.meaning: A pirate buries his letters under a <part>double mound</part> of sand, then whacks the top flat with a <part>golf club</part> so nobody can dig. A walrus flops down on top and refuses to budge. That's the best <kanji>seal</kanji> he could wish for.
封.on: He closes his lunch box just as tight, so no gull can steal his <sound>foo</sound>d.

騒.meaning: At a garden party, a <part>horse</part> is munching a giant <part>pretzel</part> when an <part>insect</part> crawls into his ear. He bucks, neighs, kicks over the punch bowl and gallops round the lawn with the band chasing him. It's the most <kanji>boisterous</kanji> party of the year.
騒.on: Someone slips on a bar of <sound>soa</sound>p and slides under the table, giggling.
騒.kun: The guests dance to loud <sound>sa</sound>lsa and yell '<sound>Wah</sound>!' until the neighbours bang on the wall.

侵.meaning: Your roommate hangs his coat on your <part>coat hook</part>. Next day his <part>rake</part> leans in your corner, then his <part>blanket</part> creeps onto your bed, and a half-eaten <part>pretzel</part> turns up on your pillow. Inch by inch, his stuff starts to <kanji>encroach</kanji>.
侵.on: One night you stub your <sound>shin</sound> on his rake in the dark.
侵.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' you yell, and chop his pretzel in half with a <sound>ka</sound>rate chop.
